implementation_notes: The default Java realization: the interface (and any value types it mentions) lives in a contract package or module that both sides depend on, while the implementing class stays in an implementation package that is not exported. The composition root instantiates the implementation and passes the interface type into clients. No service discovery machinery is involved, so failures are compile-time or immediate start-up failures.
pitfalls: A public interface in a package that also contains implementation classes exposes the implementation types to anyone reading the module.
Interfaces compiled against Java 8 can still be implemented by newer code, but adding abstract methods later breaks every implementor (use default methods or a new interface).
Reflection-based wiring (Class.forName) moves failures to runtime; prefer explicit construction or a container.

variants.name: JPMS service provider (ServiceLoader + provides/uses)
variants.implementation_notes: The deployment reading of the pattern at module level: the contract module exports the service interface, the consumer declares uses, and each provider module declares provides ... with ..., so the implementation can be added to the module path after the client was compiled. ServiceLoader instantiates providers in the order the module descriptor lists them; this is the form to choose for plugin-style extension points.
pitfalls: The provider module must not export the implementation package, or clients can bypass the service contract.
There is no support for a module declaring a provider that lives in another module, so the provider class must be local to the module that provides it.
Ordering of providers from different modules is undefined; do not rely on discovery order for selection.
